gloss: drive out, thrust out; divorced woman; open land round a city
summary: גָּרַשׁ is to drive someone out by force from where they were: the man from the garden (Gen 3:24), Cain from the ground, Hagar and her son from Abraham’s house, Israel from Egypt, and above all the nations of Canaan, whom Yahweh drives out before Israel little by little until Israel possesses the land (Exo 23:29–30). Its passive participle גְּרוּשָׁה is the woman driven out from her husband, the divorced woman whom a priest may not marry (Lev 21:7). The noun מִגְרָשׁ is the open land round the Levites’ cities and round the sanctuary and city of Ezekiel’s vision, kept for their cattle; how it ties to “drive out” is not shown. Ugaritic and Phoenician grš are “drive out, expel”, and Paul quotes Sarah’s “cast out the bondwoman and her son” (Gen 21:10) in Gal 4:30.

words.gloss: open land, pasture land round a city
words.summary: The open ground outside a city wall, measured out round the Levites’ forty-eight cities for their cattle and goods (Num 35:2–5), and round the sanctuary and the city in Ezekiel’s portion. Scripture does not show how it ties to the verb’s “drive out”, and no cognate has the noun; the link to the root is not yet understood.

senses.gloss: open land round the Levites’ cities
senses.definition: The land round each city given to the Levites, measured outward from the wall, for their cattle, their goods and their beasts; it belonged to the Levites for ever and could not be sold.

evidence.note: Israel is to give the Levites cities to dwell in, and מִגְרָשׁ for the cities round about them.
The cities are to dwell in, and their מִגְרְשֵׁיהֶם are for their cattle, their goods and all their beasts.
It is measured “from the wall of the city and outward”, a thousand cubits round about.
Two thousand cubits on each side, the city in the midst: “this shall be to them the מִגְרְשֵׁי of the cities”.
Forty-eight cities, “them and their מִגְרְשֵׁיהֶן”.
The Levites had no portion in the land “except cities to dwell in, and their מִגְרְשֵׁיהֶם for their cattle and their substance”.
“The field of the מִגְרַשׁ of their cities shall not be sold, for it is their possession for ever.”
The Levites claim the cities with their מִגְרְשֵׁיהֶן, as Yahweh commanded by Moses.
“These cities were each a city and its מִגְרָשׁ round about it; so for all these cities.”
The sons of Gershon receive Golan in Bashan and its מִגְרָשׁ.
Israel gave the Levites the cities and their מִגְרְשֵׁיהֶם.
The priests and Levites “in their cities of מִגְרְשֵׁיהֶם”.
Under Jeroboam the Levites left their מִגְרְשֵׁיהֶם and their possession and came to Judah.
“The fields of the מִגְרַשׁ of their cities.”

senses.gloss: open land round a sanctuary or city
senses.definition: In Ezekiel’s portion, a strip of open ground left round the sanctuary, and round the city as common land, neither holy nor built on.

evidence.note: Of the holy place: a square of five hundred, “and fifty cubits מִגְרָשׁ for it round about”.
The rest of the strip is common (חֹל) for the city, “for dwelling and for מִגְרָשׁ”.
The city’s מִגְרָשׁ is two hundred and fifty cubits to the north, south, east and west.

senses.definition: More widely, the open lands of a region or round a city: the pasture lands of Sharon, the outlying lands of Tyre that shake at the cry of its pilots. In Ezk 36:5 the form may instead be the verb’s infinitive, “to drive it out”.

evidence.note: Gad dwelt in Gilead and Bashan “and in all the מִגְרְשֵׁי of Sharon”.
At the cry of Tyre’s pilots the מִגְרֹשׁוֹת shake: the open lands round the city.
The nations took Yahweh’s land for a possession לְמַעַן מִגְרָשָׁהּ לָבַז, “so that its open land should be a prey”, or, read as the verb, “to drive it out for a prey”.

evidence.locator: מִגְרָשׁ → ἀφορίζω ×39, περισπόρια ×57 (lemma counts, MACULA alignment)
evidence.note: The Septuagint renders it by τὰ ἀφωρισμένα, “the lands marked off”, or περισπόρια, “the lands round about”; neither is evidence of the Hebrew’s meaning.
“Set apart (ἀφορίσατε) for me Barnabas and Saul.”
Paul “set apart (ἀφωρισμένος) to the gospel of God”.

phrases.gloss: and its open land: the refrain of the Levites’ city lists

stems.gloss: drive out; cast up; (passive participle) divorced woman

senses.definition: Once in the active participle, of Yahweh driving the nations out of the land before Israel, as the piel elsewhere.

evidence.note: “Behold, I am driving out (גֹרֵשׁ) before you the Amorite, the Canaanite …”

senses.definition: Of the restless sea, to throw up what is in it onto the shore.

evidence.note: The wicked are like the tossed sea that cannot rest, “and its waters cast up (וַיִּגְרְשׁוּ) mire and mud”.

senses.definition: גְּרוּשָׁה, a woman driven out by her husband, put away from his house: named with the widow, and forbidden as a wife to the priests.

evidence.note: A priest shall not take “a woman driven out from her husband” (אִשָּׁה גְּרוּשָׁה מֵאִישָׁהּ), for he is holy to his God.
The high priest shall not take a widow or a גְּרוּשָׁה, but a virgin of his own people.
A priest’s daughter who is a widow or גְּרוּשָׁה, with no child, returns to her father’s house as in her youth and may eat of his bread.
The vow of a widow or a גְּרוּשָׁה stands against her: she has no husband to annul it.
The priests of Ezekiel’s temple shall not take a widow or a גְּרוּשָׁה, only virgins or a priest’s widow.

senses.definition: To be put out from someone’s presence.

evidence.note: From the belly of the fish: “I am driven out (נִגְרַשְׁתִּי) from before your eyes; yet I will look again toward your holy temple.”

senses.definition: Of the sea and the Nile, to be thrown up and about, never at rest.

evidence.note: “Like the tossed sea (כַּיָּם נִגְרָשׁ), for it cannot be quiet.”
The land shall rise up wholly like the Nile, “and be tossed and sink”, like the river of Egypt.

senses.gloss: drive out (the nations from their land)
senses.definition: Of Yahweh (or the hornet or angel he sends), to drive the peoples of Canaan out of their land before Israel, so that Israel may take it; done little by little, and withheld when Israel disobeyed. Also of enemies seeking to drive Israel out of its land.

evidence.note: “I will not drive them out from before you in one year, lest the land become desolate.”
“Little by little I will drive them out from before you, until you are increased and possess the land.”
“You brought a vine out of Egypt; you drove out the nations and planted it”: driving out, against planting.
“He drove out the nations before them, and allotted them an inheritance by line.”
The hornet will drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite and the Hittite.
“You shall drive them out before you.”
“I will send an angel before you, and I will drive out the Canaanite …”
“He thrust out the enemy from before you, and said, Destroy.”
“I sent the hornet before you, which drove them out … not with your sword nor with your bow.”
“Yahweh drove out from before us all the peoples.”
“I drove them out before you and gave you their land.”
Because Israel made covenants with them: “I will not drive them out before you; they shall be as thorns in your sides.”
God went to redeem a people for himself, “to drive out nations from before your people”.
Balak wants Israel cursed, “that I may drive them out of the land”.
Ammon, Moab and Seir come “to drive us out of your possession, which you gave us to inherit”.
Stephen: the tent came in with Joshua “into the possession of the nations whom God thrust out (ἐξῶσεν) before the face of our fathers”.

senses.gloss: drive out (from a place, house or presence)
senses.definition: To put a person out of where he lives or belongs, by force or command: the man from the garden, Cain from the ground, a son from his father’s house, a priest from his office, Israel from Yahweh’s house.

evidence.note: “So he drove out the man”, and set cherubim to keep the way of the tree of life; Gen 3:23 has “sent him forth” (שִׁלַּח).
Cain: “You have driven me out this day from the face of the ground, and from your face I shall be hid.”
Gilead’s sons drove out Jephthah: “You shall not inherit in our father’s house.”
David: “they have driven me out this day from cleaving to the inheritance of Yahweh, saying, Go, serve other gods.”
Solomon drove out Abiathar from being priest to Yahweh, fulfilling the word against the house of Eli.
“Because of the wickedness of their deeds I will drive them out of my house; I will love them no more.”
Zebul drove out Gaal and his brothers, so that they should not dwell in Shechem.
The shepherds drove away Reuel’s daughters from the well.
Moses and Aaron were driven out from Pharaoh’s presence.
David feigned madness before Abimelech, “who drove him away, and he went”.
“Drive out the scorner, and contention will go out, and strife and reproach will cease.”
Of the cedar Assyria: “I have driven him out for his wickedness.”
“Ashdod, they shall drive her out at noon, and Ekron shall be rooted up.”

senses.gloss: turn out of house and home
senses.definition: To evict the weak from their homes and possessions, a wrong the prophets condemn.

evidence.note: “The women of my people you drive out from their pleasant houses.”

senses.gloss: cast out, send away for good
senses.definition: To thrust someone out of a household or a land with no return: the bondwoman and her son from Abraham’s house, Israel from Egypt.

evidence.note: Sarah: “Cast out (גָּרֵשׁ) this bondwoman and her son, for the son of this bondwoman shall not inherit with my son, with Isaac.” Quoted in Gal 4:30.
“What does the scripture say? Cast out (ἔκβαλε) the bondwoman and her son.”
“With a strong hand he shall drive them out of his land.”
“When he lets you go, he will surely thrust you out (גָּרֵשׁ יְגָרֵשׁ) from here altogether”, beside שִׁלַּח “let go”.

senses.definition: To be thrust out, with no time to delay, or out of the company of men.

evidence.note: They baked unleavened cakes, “because they were thrust out of Egypt and could not tarry”.
“They are driven out from among men; they cry after them as after a thief.”

evidence.locator: גָּרַשׁ → ἐκβάλλω (lemma) ×22 and as unlemmatised ἐκβαλῶ, ἐκβαλεῖ ×11 (MACULA alignment); Gen.21.10 גָּרֵשׁ → ἔκβαλε; Lev.21.7 גְּרוּשָׁה → ἐκβεβλημένην

evidence.note: Paul quotes Gen 21:10: “Cast out (ἔκβαλε) the bondwoman and her son, for the son of the bondwoman shall not inherit with the son of the free woman.”
“The sons of the kingdom shall be cast out (ἐκβληθήσονται) into the outer darkness.”
“When you see Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, and yourselves cast out (ἐκβαλλομένους).”
“Him who comes to me I will by no means cast out (ἐκβάλω ἔξω).”

parallels.note: Send away: set beside גֵּרֵשׁ of the man sent out of the garden and of Pharaoh letting Israel go.
Be uprooted: Ekron uprooted as Ashdod is driven out.
The widow, named with the divorced woman as a woman with no husband.

opposites.note: Plant: the nations driven out, Israel planted in their place.
Possess: the nations driven out until Israel possesses the land.
Be quiet: the tossed sea cannot be quiet.

phrases.gloss: a woman driven out from her husband: a divorced woman
he will surely drive out (infinitive with finite verb)

words.summary: Once, in Moses’ blessing of Joseph, set beside “the produce of the sun”: what the months put forth. Its tie to the root is the qal’s “cast up” (Isa 57:20), what is thrown out; no cognate has the noun, so the link rests on that one verse.

senses.definition: What the land puts forth month by month, set in parallel with the produce the sun brings.

evidence.note: “With the precious things of the produce (תְּבוּאֹת) of the sun, and with the precious things of the גֶּרֶשׁ of the months (יְרָחִים).”

words.summary: Once, in the plural: the princes’ driving of the people out of their holdings, the act the piel names in Mic 2:9.

senses.definition: The princes’ acts of driving people out of their homes and land, named with violence and spoil.

evidence.note: “Put away violence and spoil, do judgment and righteousness; take away your גְּרֻשֹׁתֵיכֶם from my people.”
The same wrong in other words: the prince shall not take the people’s inheritance “to thrust them out of their possession”.

words.summary: The Syriac verb, once in the New Testament (Revelation, which the BFBS text supplies from a later Syriac version), where the dragon’s tail drags a third of the stars. “Drag” is not “drive out”; whether it is the same word, force moving something from its place, is not shown, and its only cognates (Jewish Aramaic “hoist up”, Akkadian “move towards”) are uncertain.

evidence.note: “His tail drags (גָּרְשָׁא, Greek σύρει) a third of the stars of heaven.”

cognates.note: A marzeaḥ (cult association) contract has the host say “and if I drive you out (agrškm) from my house”, with b “from” as Hebrew has מִן: the use of Jdg 11:7 and Hos 9:15. Ugaritic keeps š and ṯ apart, and has š.

evidence.note: “/ʾagarrišu-kum(u)/, imperf. 1. sing. D (factitive) /g-r-š/ ‘to drive out’ with suff. 2. pl. m.”; “/bi-bêti-ya/ b- in the sense ‘from’ after /g-r-š/”.
“agrškm ‘to drive out’ (H. g-r-š Qal part. and Pi.)”.

cognates.note: Phoenician has the niphal “it was driven out” of a garrison expelled from Sardinia (CIS i 144), and Neo-Punic in Latin letters garasth “I drove out” the wicked fellow: the Hebrew piel’s and niphal’s use.

evidence.note: “v. qal EXPEL, DRIVE OUT. CIS i 144.1/3 (Ph) … ngrš hʾ bšrdn, ‘It was driven out from Sardinia.’ … (NPu) … garasth … ‘From Adnim I drove out the wicked fellow’.”

cognates.gloss: (pael) send away, divorce; (ithpeel) be divorced (Jewish Babylonian Aramaic)
cognates.note: The Talmud’s Aramaic for putting away a wife, as the Hebrew’s passive participle גְּרוּשָׁה is the divorced woman. It may echo the rabbinic Hebrew it sits beside.

evidence.note: “Pa. גָּרֵישׁ. Pes. 110ᵇ דגָרְשָׁהּ לאיתתיה who had divorced his wife … Ithpe. … to be divorced.”

cognates.note: Jastrow sets it beside גרר “drag”. With the Syriac “drag” it suggests a pulling sense in Aramaic, against Hebrew’s driving out; one or two uses only.

evidence.note: “(cmp. גרר to drag) to hoist up. Y. Kil. IX, 32ᶜ … ‘and if I call, ye will hoist me up’.”

evidence.locator: SEM000093 grš [eject] V, ARM006498 GRŠ [pull] V

cognates.note: Five Neo-Assyrian and later attestations, glossed “move towards, copulating”. A motion verb, but not driving away; not checked in CAD.

evidence.locator: SEM000093 grš [eject] V, AKK002806 garāšu [move] V

doctrine.statement: Yahweh God said the man must not “put forth his hand and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever”; so he sent him out of the garden and drove him out (וַיְגָרֶשׁ), and set cherubim to keep the way of the tree of life (Gen 3:22–24). He had been told “in the day you eat of it you shall surely die” and “to dust you shall return” (Gen 2:17; 3:19). From the verses: the man was not made immortal, for life for ever is what he was driven away from; and the way back to it is what Christ promises: “to him who overcomes I will give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of God” (Rev 2:7), and “blessed are they who do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life” (Rev 22:14).

Sarah said, “Cast out (גָּרֵשׁ) this bondwoman and her son, for the son of this bondwoman shall not inherit with my son, with Isaac”, and God told Abraham to hearken to her, “for in Isaac shall your seed be called” (Gen 21:10–12). Driving out is losing the inheritance: Jephthah’s brothers drove him out saying “you shall not inherit in our father’s house” (Jdg 11:2), and David was driven out “from cleaving to the inheritance of Yahweh” (1Sa 26:19). Paul quotes Sarah’s words as what the scripture says: the bondwoman is the covenant from Sinai, Isaac’s children are the children of promise, and “the son of the bondwoman shall not inherit with the son of the free woman” (Gal 4:22–31). Jesus says many will come from east and west and sit down with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom, while the sons of the kingdom are cast out (Mat 8:11–12; Luk 13:28–29), yet “him who comes to me I will by no means cast out” (Jhn 6:37). From the verses: the inheritance promised to Abraham is received by promise, in Isaac’s line, not by birth after the flesh or by the law; those who hold to the law in place of the promise are driven out from it, as Ishmael was.

Yahweh promised to drive out the nations of Canaan before Israel himself, by the hornet and by his angel (Exo 23:28; 33:2), “little by little … until you are increased and possess the land”, lest the land become desolate and the beasts multiply (Exo 23:29–30). Joshua told Israel it was done “not with your sword nor with your bow” (Jos 24:12), and Israel answered “Yahweh drove out from before us all the peoples … we too will serve Yahweh” (Jos 24:18). When Israel made covenants with those peoples he said “I will not drive them out before you” (Jdg 2:1–3). Stephen speaks of “the nations whom God thrust out before the face of our fathers” (Act 7:45). From the verses: Israel held the land as Yahweh’s gift, given by his driving out its peoples, and its holding hung on serving him.

note: Root key גרש, as the corpus keys it. Left out: the names גֵּרְשׁוֹן Gershon (c.di.ae, with the gentilic גֵּרְשֻׁנִּי c.di.af, both in names/gershon.json) and גֵּרְשֹׁם Gershom (c.di.ad, not entered; Exo 2:22 explains it by גֵּר “sojourner” and שָׁם “there”, so its tie to this root is a question for its own entry; c.di.ad and c.di.ae share six tokens, Num 3:21, 26:57; 1Ch 6:56, 15:7, 23:6, 26:24). m.ak.af (מִגְרָשׁ as “vb, see גרשׁ”) has no tokens and is a cross-reference. The qal passive participle גְּרוּשָׁה “divorced” has no key of its own and is a sense of the qal. Arabic: the regular correspondence would be جرس, which Lane gives as “make a sound” (pp. 409–410), and جرث is a fish (p. 404); neither shares a meaning, so no Arabic cognate is recorded. Ugaritic: the club named ygrš “Driver” (KTU 1.2 IV 11–12) is a strong lead, but Segert’s selection omits lines 11–17 and DULAT is not available; not cited. Ge’ez (Leslau, Dillmann), CAD G for garāšu, Payne Smith for Syriac ܓܪܫ not consulted. Syriac: SEDRA root 408 has one lexeme, 633 גרש “drag; draw”; its only BFBS token is Rev 12:4. Phoenician form is from Krahmalkov p. 143, read from the PDF’s OCR (G-R-S, š lost); check the scan. Greek for מִגְרָשׁ: ἀφορίζω is recorded only as the Septuagint’s bridge word; its NT uses (set apart) have nothing to do with the open land, and περισπόρια is not in the NT; review whether to drop it. Open: (1) Ezk 36:5 מִגְרָשָׁהּ, noun or infinitive. (2) Whether מִגְרָשׁ belongs to this root at all; the link is unexplained. (3) The Syriac “drag” is kept as a word of the entry on spelling; review.
